Yes. Based on the snapshot, paid acquisition is viable enough to test; CAC is not the obvious bottleneck right now. The reason is that acquisition has to be read through CAC, gross profit, and payback together [how-businesses-make-money:2]. Here, CAC is about $1,000 and first-30-day gross profit is about $10,000, so first-month gross profit is far above acquisition cost. That clears the client-financed acquisition threshold where first-30-day gross profit is greater than CAC [cfa:0], and the deterministic CFA check classifies this as Level 3.

The caveat is that the current $1,000 CAC came from referral partners, not proven paid ads. So I would interpret this as permission to run a controlled paid-acquisition test, not proof that every paid channel will hold. The thing to watch is whether paid traffic keeps CAC low enough and payback fast enough, because shorter payback is what makes advertising easier to scale [payback-period:0].
